data.text: Now I understand the codebase. Let me set up a task list and build the graph view.

data.summary: pnpm lint 2>&1 | tail -20 && echo "=== tsc ui ===" && pnpm t

data.text:
Task 6 complete. `pnpm verify` exits 0.

**What I built** — the capability archive graph view under `packages/ui/src/graph/` (13 files, all ≤ 250 lines), replacing only the graph placeholder in `app.tsx`:

- **Pure, testable core**: `graphControlsReducer` (independent rejected/reads/depends/fill fields + capability selection), `fillValue` (summed non-null execution+planning cost with summed coverage; missing stays null; attempts direct), `orderedArchived` (valid landed dates, timestamp then key), `graphLayout` (capability-ordered lanes, one time scale with per-location ordinal offsets, active right gutter, rejected band behind its toggle, one mark per change with a connector across every written lane, node-count content floor), and `projectRelationships` (separate depends/reads layers).
- **Presentation**: `GraphControlsBar` (native checkboxes/radios with visible labels), `CapabilityPanel` (complete spec text after selection), `ChangeMark` (title + aria-label with every required field, focusable, Enter/Space activation), `GraphCanvas` (labeled horizontally scrollable SVG, separate relationship groups, legend, missing/partial patterns).
- **Tests**: `tests/ui-graph.test.tsx` — 20 tests covering all seven acceptance lines without a DOM-test dependency or network access.

**Verification**: `pnpm verify` → CLI + UI typecheck, production UI build, 1220 Node tests, 51 UI tests, Biome clean over 281 files.

**Notable deviations** (documented in the result file): SVG marks/lane headers are focusable and keyboard-activatable but omit `role="button"` to satisfy Biome's `useSemanticElements`; the scroll region is a labeled `<section>`; archived changes with invalid landed dates are omitted while active/rejected are placed regardless; lane-less changes land in an unmapped row. No drift against capability specs, no core or runtime-dependency changes.
